summary.text: The 12 Nov Elevated alert still stands: Nvidia's 8-K says Jensen Huang resigned as CEO effective 11 Nov, with the CFO as interim CEO and results still due 17 Nov (V), and Nebius moved 2026 revenue to the low end of $3.0–3.4bn and pushed its ARR target to February (V). Nebius's interim financials, filed after the 12 Nov close, show unnamed customers at 33%, 22% and 15% of Q3 revenue, one customer holding 75% of $4.04bn of receivables (up from $0.72bn at end-2025), and debt of about $14.2bn versus about $4.1bn at end-2025 (V, sums (d)); the filing shows no Nvidia or Microsoft guarantee or backstop. A Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision said on 10 Nov that AI-related debt is on track to exceed $800bn this year and that lease, contract and residual-value obligations are more than three times that, describing 'the appearance of circular financing' (V). On 12 Nov Nvidia closed 4.3% lower, Nebius 16.8% lower and CoreWeave 6.9% lower, while CoreWeave's 2032 bond recovered to about 82 by the evening (U); a DOJ antitrust probe focused on Nvidia was reported by one outlet with no company or DOJ confirmation (U). A reported OpenAI raise of $15bn at a $1.25tn valuation has not closed and conflicts with talk of a larger round (U), and no publishable dated CDS print after 10 Nov was available.
summary.source: AI Alert morning scan 13 Nov 2026 (~05:30–05:39 Europe/Zurich), independently checked ~05:38 Europe/Zurich; SEC EDGAR filings, BIS-hosted Fed speech text, public news relays

items.title: ECB letter on circular financing in the AI ecosystem
items.tier_relevance: Official qualitative flag. No new quantified euro-area exposures.
items.relationship: Flags interlinked ownership and mutual commitments, and debt-like off-balance-sheet lease or purchase commitments.

sources.title: Lagarde letter to MEPs Heinäluoma and Fernández, 6 Nov 2026, L/CL/26/245

items.notes: States that rising debt levels are 'compounded by circular financing arrangements in the form of interlinked ownership structures and mutual commitments between firms in the AI ecosystem,' and that debt financing increasingly includes 'debt-like off-balance sheet commitments to lease or purchase AI infrastructure.' Euro-area entities' exposure to AI-related debt 'remains low for now'; main spillover channels in a shock would be falling equity valuations and contagion. No significant spillover from hyperscaler euro issuance to EU government funding costs so far.

figures.note: About 4.25 GW IT load at the PORTS Technology Campus, Pike County, Ohio. Triggered on certain tenant defaults (OpenAI insolvency resulting in a lease default, or failure to pay). First phases expected fiscal 2029; payment obligations expected to begin as sites become ready for service from 2028. OpenAI has agreed to reimburse and indemnify Nvidia for amounts actually paid.

combined_links.title: Token volume is still rising; financing is the tighter constraint
combined_links.text: The 8 Nov token-demand pack shows OpenRouter's complete week of 26 Oct at a series high of 193.6T tokens (d) and Portkey tokens +15.3% week on week (d). The circular-financing scan's 11 Nov morning result is that the binding stress is funding conditions, not a measured drop in token use: CoreWeave said it does not intend to issue more parent-level unsecured debt at current yields (V), the 9 Nov bank-reluctance item remains unverified (U), and Oracle closed a $20bn equity-and-notes raise on 4 Nov (V).

combined_links.title: Volume is outpacing spend and revenue per token
combined_links.text: Ramp Tokenomics: volume +37.1% vs spend +8.9% for the week to 23 Oct versus 25 Sep (V, table unchanged through 8 Nov). Portkey: tokens +15.3% vs cost +4.4% in the week of 1 Nov (d). In the Ramp TSM chart sample, volume +64.6% vs spend +1.5% since the week of 27 Jul (d, 18 Oct vintage). The same pressure shows up in Anthropic's unit economics: compute and infrastructure expense was $9.9bn on $17.0bn of Q3 revenue, 58.2% (d) versus 48% in Q2, from the 2 Nov S-1/A.

combined_links.title: Suppliers are also financing their customers
combined_links.text: Anthropic's $26bn concurrent placement (V) is being bought by Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC — several of whom are also compute or component counterparties to ~$900.9bn of commitments (V). Nvidia's 10-Q caps SB Energy / OpenAI residual-value guarantees at $105bn (V, contingent, first phases fiscal 2029). SoftBank guarantees an SVF2 loan secured on OpenAI preferred shares (V), so a mark-down of OpenAI hits both SoftBank earnings and a liquidity clause. These structures can keep capex and measured token demand going even if outside funding tightens — and they can transmit a funding or valuation shock back through the same chain.

caveats: 12–13 Nov: 12 Nov closes (NVDA $166.19, −4.34%; NBIS $128.64, −16.84%; CRWV $56.60, −6.86%; ORCL $127.11, −0.99%) are from exchange data APIs and news quotes (U). No publishable dated CDS print after 10 Nov. CoreWeave's 2032 bond printed around 80.75 at 15:26 CET and about 82 at 22:15 CET on 12 Nov (TRACE, U). The reported DOJ antitrust probe of Nvidia is single-source (U). OpenAI round size is conflicting ($15bn per CNBC versus talk of a $30bn round, both U, no primary confirmation). Nebius customers C, D and E are unnamed in the filing; mapping them to Microsoft, Meta or others would be speculation, and the filing does not explain the receivables jump.

V means a primary document was opened in the saved independent checks (SEC filings, issuer IR, official BIS/ECB PDFs). U is secondary, anonymous, undated or not independently confirmed. (d) is an arithmetic combination of stated figures.

No dated CoreWeave, Nvidia, Oracle or Nebius CDS print was obtained after 10 Nov. A CoreWeave 2032 bond printed around 80.75 at 15:26 CET on 12 Nov (TRACE, U). Conflicting or undated secondary credit-market prints from commercial terminals or broker-sourced media are excluded; they are treated as a data gap.
Debt totals depend on the definition (recourse vs non-recourse, whether leases are included). CoreWeave's $46.873bn is recourse + non-recourse only (d from V components).

CoreWeave's Q3 10-Q was filed on 12 Nov (accepted 13:20 CET). Customer concentration and debt figures above use that filing (V). The 10-Q discloses the 14 Aug adoption of the CEO's Rule 10b5-1 plan, not a cancellation; the reported cancellation remains CNBC only (U).

OpenAI funding size and valuation are still secondary. A 12 Nov CNBC report of a $15bn raise at a $1.25tn valuation has not been independently confirmed, and no issuer-primary confirmation was in the saved files.

BIS 137 percentages are document findings; the proprietary PitchBook/FactSet microdata were not replicated. 'Circular' there is a relational classification over 2021–2025, not proof of a closed cash loop on one deal.
Call quotes use the official CoreWeave IR transcript. Press paraphrases that say 'financing' instead of 'capital', or that collapse two different 75% denominators, are not used.
This page is a research compilation, not an investment recommendation, a credit rating or a trading signal. Times are Europe/Zurich.
Saved review packs include screenshots of third-party documents or sites and charts built on credit-terminal or licensed prints; those images are not shown. Official-flag figures appear as a table.

Item tone (positive / neutral / negative) is a derived classification of circular-financing risk for this page (positive = de-risking or healthy financing; negative = rising circularity, stress or credit risk; neutral = mixed or informational). It is not a credit rating.
